extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students, graduate students, and professional mathematicians interested in contributing to the Encyclopedia of Mathematics wiki
extracted.subtask_short: contributing to Encyclopedia of Mathematics wiki
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and invitations for people (students and professionals) to join and contribute to the Encyclopedia of Mathematics wiki by retyping, updating, correcting, adding media, or creating new entries; explains provenance and technical/organizational aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you are an undergraduate student, a graduate student or a professional mathematician you are welcome to join us in this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project is explicitly open-access and welcomes contributors at many stages of training/career; anyone may create an account to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of contribution tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: From the routine task of retyping old pages in Tex to the one of updating the contents and correcting mistakes; from adding to the pages nice new media (pictures and videos) to creating completely new entries encompassing the last exciting developments of math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions can range from low-effort technical fixes (retyping formulas) to substantive content creation and multimedia enhancement; choose tasks according to skill and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical requirement: TeX proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also very easy to use: if you know Tex you will be able to write new pages in a few minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge of TeX is emphasized as enabling fast and effective page creation and editing; absence of TeX skills does not preclude participation but may limit speed/efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight and community editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike other wikis, there is an editorial board monitoring the various pages, but just like other wikis anybody who makes a user account is free to discuss and modify things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits are subject to oversight by an editorial board, so contributors should expect review; at the same time, discussion and modification by registered users is permitted, implying a mix of open editing and editorial control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance and source material
rubrics_metrics.description: The original articles are from the online Encyclopedia of Mathematics, published by Kluwer Academic Publishers in 2002. The original articles go back to the Soviet Matematicheskaya entsiklopedya (1977), originally edited by Ivan Matveevich Vinogradov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should be aware that much content derives from earlier published encyclopedias; respect for original attributions and careful updating (rather than blind replacement) is implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing technical limitation: formulas as images
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic version had its formulae written in TEX, but its code was lost: most of the current pages have the formulas saved as png images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical improvement task is to recover or retype formulas in TeX to replace PNG images, improving accessibility and editability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cases of the wiki (what makes it valuable)
rubrics_metrics.description: But of course, even if you do not want to become a contributor, just give it sometimes a try if you are looking for quick explanations, definitions, history or references: I am confident you will find out it is a great tool to learn math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The wiki is positioned as a graduate-level reference and a learning tool; contributors should aim to maintain clarity, accurate definitions, historical notes, and references to preserve its value for learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ease of access and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Anybody who makes a user account is free to discuss and modify things. It is also very easy to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation requires creating a user account; the platform is described as user-friendly, lowering the barrier to entry for edits and discussion.
